committee_name.text: Peripheral and Central Nervous System(s) Drugs Advisory Committee (PCNS AC)

quote.quote: The suvorexant NDA was considered at a meeting of the Peripheral and Central Nervous System Advisory Committee on May 22, 2013, and had the following major recommendations:
Advisory Committee Meeting: An advisory meeting was held May 22, 2013. A second advisory committee meeting was not needed for this application.

recommendation.text: The committee found substantial evidence of efficacy for sleep onset (12 yes / 4 no) and sleep maintenance (16 yes / 0 no); voted that the 15 mg and 20 mg doses were acceptably safe as initial doses (15 yes / 3 no); voted that an additional study of the 10 mg dose was not necessary to establish its efficacy (11 no / 5 yes / 1 abstention); and was divided on whether the 30 mg and 40 mg doses were adequately safe (7 yes / 8 no).

quote.quote: Most Committee members agreed that doses of 15 mg and 20 mg were acceptably safe, by a vote of 15 yes/ 3 no.

linkages.concern: The committee endorsed that the lowest effective dose should be recommended as the initial (starting) dose and generally concluded that the 10 mg dose was effective, even though a 10 mg strength was not part of the originally proposed/available product.
linkages.change: FDA concluded suvorexant could not be marketed with an acceptable safety profile without a 10 mg dose and required (via a Complete Response letter) that the 10 mg dose (plus a 5 mg dose) be made available; the resubmitted, approved product adds the lower 5 mg and 10 mg tablet strengths with 10 mg as the starting dose.

concern_quote.quote: On the one hand, they clearly voted that the 15 and 20 mg doses were acceptably safe to be recommended as starting doses. On the other hand, though, they endorsed the view that the lowest effective dose should be recommended, at least as a starting dose, and, further, they in general concluded that 10 mg was an effective dose.

change_quote.quote: Given that this dosage strength is not currently available, we believe that the Agency should issue a Complete Response (CR) letter, requiring that the 10 mg dose be available.

linkages.concern: The committee was divided on whether the higher 30 mg and 40 mg doses were adequately safe (7 voting yes, 8 voting no).
linkages.change: The 30 mg and 40 mg doses were not recommended/approved; the sponsor withdrew the 30 mg and 40 mg dosage strengths from the dosage and administration section of labeling.

concern_quote.quote: The Committee was of divided opinion about if safety was adequate for the 30 mg and 40 mg doses, with 7 voting 'yes', and 8 voting 'no'.

change_quote.quote: The sponsor has withdrawn the 30 mg and 40 mg dosage strengths from the dosage and administration section of labeling.

summary: An advisory committee meeting (Peripheral and Central Nervous System Drugs Advisory Committee) was held May 22, 2013 during the first review cycle; no transcript is in paperclip, and no second meeting was convened for the resubmission that led to the 2014 approval. The committee voted that efficacy was established and that the 15 mg and 20 mg doses were acceptably safe, endorsed using the lowest effective dose as the starting dose, generally judged 10 mg effective, and split on the safety of the 30 mg and 40 mg doses. FDA required (via a Complete Response letter) that lower 5 mg and 10 mg strengths be made available before approval, and the higher 30 mg and 40 mg doses were withdrawn from labeling.
